arml-2012-relay-1-1.title: Repeating base-7 expansion
arml-2012-relay-1-1.body:
To make $r$ as large as possible take $A=6$, and then (as $B\ne A$) $B=5$: $r=0.\overline{65}_7$.

A two-digit repeating block in base 7 means $r=\frac{65_7}{7^2-1}=\frac{6\cdot7+5}{48}=\frac{47}{48}$, already reduced. So $p+q=95$.

**Answer: 95**

arml-2012-relay-1-2.title: Angle sum in triangle AMC
arml-2012-relay-1-2.body:
*(In the relay, $T$ was the answer to the previous problem, 95.)*

$\angle ACB=U^\circ$, so $\angle BAC=(180-2U)^\circ$ and $\angle MAC=\frac{180-2U}{3}=\left(60-\frac23U\right)^\circ$. In $\triangle AMC$:
$$\left(60-\tfrac23U\right)+U+T=180\implies \tfrac13U=120-T\implies U=3(120-T).$$
With $T=95$: $U=75$.

**Answer: 75**

arml-2012-relay-1-3.title: Difference of binomial coefficients
arml-2012-relay-1-3.body:
*(In the relay, $T$ was the answer to the previous problem, 75.)*

$$\binom{n+2}{2}-\binom n2=\frac{(n+2)(n+1)-n(n-1)}{2}=\frac{4n+2}{2}=2n+1=T.$$
So $n=\frac{T-1}2=37$.

**Answer: 37**

arml-2012-relay-2-1.title: Drift by 9° every three steps
arml-2012-relay-2-1.body:
$123^\circ$ is in Quadrant II, $246^\circ$ in III, and $369^\circ\equiv9^\circ$ in I. Quadrant IV is still missing.

Since $3\cdot123^\circ=369^\circ\equiv9^\circ$, the $(k+3)$rd angle is the $k$th rotated by $9^\circ$. Starting from $246^\circ$ (which is $24^\circ$ short of $270^\circ$): the 5th angle is $255^\circ$, the 8th $264^\circ$, the 11th $273^\circ$, which is in Quadrant IV. The other sequences ($123^\circ+9j$, $9^\circ+9j$) don't reach Quadrant IV that soon. So $n=11$.

**Answer: 11**

arml-2012-relay-2-2.title: Choose digits from the last one backward
arml-2012-relay-2-2.body:
*(In the relay, $T$ was the answer to the previous problem, 11.)*

Plates have $d=T-3=8$ digits. Choose the digits from the last to the first. The $k$th digit must lie in $\{k,\dots,9\}$ ($10-k$ values), and must differ from the $d-k$ digits after it, which are distinct and all lie in $\{k+1,\dots,9\}\subset\{k,\dots,9\}$. So the $k$th digit has exactly $(10-k)-(d-k)=10-d$ choices, whatever the later digits were.

So there are $(10-d)^d=2^8=256$ plates.

**Answer: 256**

arml-2012-relay-2-3.title: Square minus circle
arml-2012-relay-2-3.body:
*(In the relay, $T$ was the answer to the previous problem, 256.)*

$|x|+|y|\le\sqrt{2T}$ is a square (rotated $45^\circ$) with half-diagonal $\sqrt{2T}$, so its area is $\frac12(2\sqrt{2T})^2=4T$. The circle $x^2+y^2=T$ has radius $\sqrt T$, which equals the square's inradius $\frac{\sqrt{2T}}{\sqrt2}$, so the circle is inscribed in the square. The area is $4T-\pi T=1024-256\pi$.

**Answer: $1024-256\pi$**
